conduct: Agent conduct (mandatory): (1) No AI attribution: no `Co-Authored-By:` trailer or "Generated by/with …" line naming an AI model, agent or tool in commit messages, PR or ticket descriptions, or comments. A human co-author, a code-generator note and a model name as technical provenance are allowed. (2) No commit, push, merge or release without an explicit ask. Invoking an orchestrator is the ask for its own task-boundary commits; merge and release always need their own ask. (3) Never destroy others' work: no `git stash` in a dirty tree, no blanket `git add -A` while parallel lanes share a checkout, no force-push to a shared branch. (4) No secrets or personal data in output, logs or commits. (5) Report honestly: name what failed, what was skipped and what was not verified.

finding.problem: Documentation drift in a symbol this delta changed. The fix for r3-logic-w5-F-002 replaced the hand-off rule. A status row now anchors to its own parent: a Loading row anchors to `d:<parent>`, and a Show more row to the parent's last entry, and focus goes to the next row of that parent (handOff(), with the layout effect's `after.find(row => row.parent === lost.parent)`). Only an entry row still uses 'the row before it'. The component doc above `export function MetaprojectTree` still states only the old rule, 'the one after the row that preceded it'. That rule is the one the new test 'a focused Show more whose page lands with the children of the folder above it…' shows to be wrong: the row before Show more there is src's Loading row. The handOff doc and the layout-effect comment in the same file give the new rule, so one behaviour is now documented two ways.
finding.impact: A reader of the component's public doc expects the pre-fix behaviour. A later change made to match that doc would bring back the r3-logic-w5-F-002 misfocus.
finding.suggested_fix: Reword the last sentence of the doc so it defers to handOff, for example: '…when the focused row is replaced (its folder or next page loaded), focus goes to the row now at its place (`handOff`): a status row hands it to its own parent's next row, any other row to the row after the one that preceded it.'
finding.evidence: MetaprojectTree.tsx:101-107 (component doc, unchanged by the delta) against handOff() at :958-965 of slice-02 (new) and the layout effect's target lookup (`lost.parent === undefined ? after[0] : after.find(row => row.parent === lost.parent)`), both changed in this delta. The new test in MetaprojectTree.dom.test.tsx expects focus on README.md, not on the row after the Loading row.
finding.quote:
* when the focused row is replaced (its folder or next page loaded), focus goes to the row now at its
 * place: the one after the row that preceded it, when that row is still shown.

premise.reasoning: The component doc at MetaprojectTree.tsx:104-106 states one hand-off rule ('the one after the row that preceded it'). handOff() at :65-79 and the layout effect at :177-180, both changed in this delta, now anchor a status row to its own parent. The two texts in one file describe one behaviour differently, and the doc's version is the one the round-3 fix replaced. No intent signal keeps the old wording: the T14 journal entry says the docs were reworded but names only the limiter and TreeFolder/ensure/more docs. Deferring the doc to handOff is a sound, local fix.

finding.problem: The `reload` doc, the MetaprojectView comment ('Every catalog load (a new catalog object) re-reads…') and the PR body ('every catalog load re-reads it') all say that any catalog load re-reads parked stale reads. The quiet re-read that runs when the explorer is shown again does not. When it finds the same snapshot, it returns before setCatalog (MetaprojectView.tsx:410-412), so `reload` does not change and the parked rows stay Loading.
finding.impact: Users are not affected. Neither does that quiet path clear snapshotMismatch, so the Refresh catalog banner is still on screen and still recovers the rows. The wording claims more than the code does.
finding.suggested_fix: Say 'every catalog load that replaces the catalog (Refresh catalog, Rebuild, a new snapshot)', or 'every user-started catalog load'.
finding.evidence: consumer-trace: MetaprojectView.tsx passes `reload: catalog` to useMetaprojectTree. The catalog effect at :410-416 calls setCatalog and setSnapshotMismatch(false) only on a non-quiet read or a changed snapshot. The reload effect in useMetaprojectTree.ts fires only on `loadedCatalog.current !== reload`.
finding.quote: * Changes whenever the explorer loads its catalog (Refresh catalog included), whether or not the

finding.problem: A stale-snapshot read is parked as status 'stale' (or more: {status: 'stale'}) and only a change of `reload` re-reads it (the useEffect comparing loadedCatalog.current to reload is the sole caller of reread(scope, parent, 'stale')). `reload` is optional: a caller that omits it has no exit from a parked row, since ensure skips present folders, more refuses a set non-failed page, and retry acts only on 'failed'. The DOM-test Harness in MetaprojectTree.dom.test.tsx omits it; MetaprojectView passes reload: catalog.
finding.impact: No user-visible defect at this head. The type does not encode the contract the round-3 major fix depends on, so a new caller or a refactor of the view's call can silently bring back the permanent Loading row.
finding.suggested_fix: Make `reload` required and pass a value from the test Harness; or, when reload is undefined, treat 'stale' like 'failed' (offer Retry) so no state lacks an exit.
finding.evidence: useMetaprojectTree.ts hook input type `reload?: unknown;`; effect `if (loadedCatalog.current === reload) return;` then reread(..., 'stale'). Callers: MetaprojectView.tsx (reload: catalog), MetaprojectTree.dom.test.tsx Harness (no reload).

premise.reasoning: `reload?: unknown` (useMetaprojectTree.ts:114) was added by this delta, so its optionality is not a prior deliberate choice. The hook doc at :103 says a stale read is parked 'until `reload` changes', and the effect at :261-268 is the only re-read of a stale park. A caller that omits the input leaves no way out of the parked state, which is the dead state of the round-3 major. Making a contract-bearing input required is ordinary TypeScript practice. Of the two fixes offered, only the first is consistent with the operator's T12/T14 decision (stale shows the Refresh catalog banner only, no Retry, per the journal). The second fix (treat stale like failed and offer Retry when reload is undefined) would contradict that decision. The fixer should take the first.

pr.title: feat(desktop): browse Metaproject files and wiki pages as a tree
pr.body:
## Summary

Flow 518. Without a search, the Metaproject sidebar is now a tree instead of a flat list of the catalog's first 200 nodes: in **Graph**, indexed files by folder (folders first, with file counts; a module folder selects its module node); in **Wiki**, pages grouped by page type. Folders load on demand, so the whole project is reachable.

- **Core:** new read-only v2 action `tree` (`scope: graph | wiki`, optional `parent`, paged with snapshot-bound cursors, `not-found` / `stale-snapshot` / `invalid-input` like the other actions). Listed in `capabilities`; v1 unchanged.
- **Transport:** Rust `RequestV2::Tree` with validation and tests. The handshake still requires only the six existing actions, so an older CLI keeps working; Desktop learns `supportsTree` from the probe.
- **Desktop:** `MetaprojectTree` (WAI-ARIA tree, roving focus, Up/Down/Left/Right/Home/End/Enter/Space), `useMetaprojectTree` (per-scope expanded set and pages, retry per folder, Show more, snapshot changes), mounted in `MetaprojectView` only with no query and a CLI that offers `tree`. A selection made elsewhere reveals its path; the item shown by default on first open does not.
- **Docs:** the Desktop Metaproject guide describes the tree, keyboard and the older-CLI behaviour.

## Review fixes

Four managed review rounds; their fixes are in this PR.

- Round 1 fixes: focus stays in the tree when a focused status row changes or leaves; tree reads are bounded to 3 in flight (Desktop's 8 read permits are shared); a v2 answer for another snapshot is refused as `stale-snapshot` in the transport for every action, so search Load more shows the Refresh catalog banner instead of "Incompatible … Choose the bundled CLI"; module folders show a **Module** label; the untyped wiki group key is one helper shared by core and Desktop.
- Round 2 fixes: focus moves to the right row when a page or two folders' answers land together; a stale-snapshot tree read shows the Refresh catalog banner and no Retry that cannot succeed (the row stays Loading… until a catalog load re-reads it, see round 3); a read refused because every permit is busy is retried twice with a short jittered wait before the folder shows the error.
- Round 3 fixes: a tree read refused as stale-snapshot is parked and every catalog load re-reads it, so Refresh catalog recovers it even when the snapshot id comes back unchanged; the read-permit refusal is classified once in the platform transport; a replaced status row hands focus within its own parent.
- Round 4 fixes: the tree's `reload` input is required (it is the only way out of a parked stale read); the focus hand-off target moved into a helper and the component doc matches it; tests pin the parked stale row, the refused Show more, a reveal through a stale folder, the Wiki re-read, the permit classifier ignoring typed CLI errors and the empty-page focus fallback; the flow plan states the current focus rule and the stale-snapshot state.

## Verification

- At the head: `cd apps/desktop && bunx tsc --noEmit && bun test src` exit 0, 1021 pass. Core tree and explorer tests pass; `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run docs:check` exit 0 (re-run after round 1; rounds 2-4 touched only Desktop).
- CI on the round-1 head ran the Rust `cargo test --locked metaproject` and passed.
- Not run: no native walkthrough of the packaged app; focus behaviour is checked in the DOM test environment only.

Flow package: `.metaproject/flows/518-2026-11-23-desktop-metaproject-sidebar-tree/`.

acceptance_criteria: - AC1: A v2 `tree` request with `scope: "graph"` returns, for the root and for any folder, the folders containing indexed files (sorted, with file counts, a module folder carrying its module node) followed by that folder's file nodes (sorted), never symbols; pages of at most 100 entries chain by `nextCursor` to the full child list with no duplicate or missing entry; `scope: "wiki"` returns page-type groups at the root and a group's pages under it. [verify: exec `bun test src/integrations/metaproject-explorer-tree.test.ts`]

- AC2: Malformed `tree` requests (unknown keys, bad scope, absolute or `..` parent, bad cursor) answer `invalid-input`; an unknown parent answers `not-found`; a cursor or `expectedSnapshotId` from another snapshot answers `stale-snapshot`; `capabilities` lists `tree`; v1 requests parse and answer exactly as before. [verify: exec `bun test src/integrations/metaproject-explorer-tree.test.ts src/integrations/metaproject-explorer.test.ts` · sensitive: failure-scenario]

- AC3: The Desktop Rust command accepts a well-formed `tree` request, refuses a malformed one, and still requires of a CLI only the six existing actions. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop/src-tauri && cargo test --locked metaproject`]

- AC4: Desktop learns from the capability probe whether the CLI offers `tree`; against a CLI that does not, the explorer negotiates successfully and the sidebar shows today's flat list with no error. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/platform/metaproject.test.ts src/metaproject/MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx` · sensitive: failure-scenario]

- AC5: The tree component renders folders, groups and node rows with WAI-ARIA tree semantics and roving focus; Up/Down/Left/Right/Home/End/Enter/Space behave as the plan states; expanding reads a folder once and shows a loading row; a failed folder read shows an inline error whose Retry re-reads only that folder; "Show more" appends the next page in order; selecting a node row calls the selection callback with that node; a graph that is not built shows an empty-state line. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/MetaprojectTree.dom.test.tsx` · sensitive: failure-scenario]

- AC6: In the explorer, the tree shows without a query and flat results with one; expanded folders and the selection survive leaving and returning to the view and switching between Graph and Wiki; a selection made elsewhere expands its ancestors and scrolls its row into view without moving focus; a new snapshot keeps the expanded set, drops stale children and answers, and never sends an old-snapshot cursor. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx`]
- AC7: The Desktop package type-checks and its whole test suite passes. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bunx tsc --noEmit && bun test src`]
- AC8: The core package lints and type-checks. [verify: exec `bun run lint && bun run typecheck`]
- AC9: The Desktop Metaproject guide describes the tree (Graph folders, Wiki groups, keyboard, behaviour with an older CLI) and the docs checks pass. [verify: exec `bun run docs:check`]
